response.text: The narrative explains the whale-line’s construction and the lethal serpentine path it takes through a boat, before plunging into Stubb’s chase: burning palms on the loggerhead, “Wet the line!” cries, the iron’s bite, the lancing, the whale’s bloody “flurry,” and the sharks’ night-feast while Stubb dines and makes old Fleece preach to the sharks. Ishmael digresses on overtaxed harpooneers, the crotch and second iron’s hazards, the “monkey-rope” binding him to Queequeg amid a pandemonium of sharks and spades, then tours cutting-in, the philosophy of blubber/skin, and the baling of the spermaceti case—where Tashtego falls and Queequeg rescues him with cool audacity. The Pequod soon carries both a sperm and a right whale’s heads, prompting meditations on their eyes, ears, foreheads, and the sperm whale’s battering-ram brow, while Ahab broods over the Sphinx-like head and the crew banters ominously about Fedallah and fate. They gam with the Jeroboam, whose fanatic Gabriel warns them after a mate dies to Moby Dick; race and mock the Jungfrau; and chase vast “gallied” herds off Sunda amid drugged whales, circling sharks, and knife-edge near-disasters. Ishmael lays down the whalemen’s property code of “Fast-Fish and Loose-Fish,” skewers royal claims to heads and tails, and watches Stubb extort ambergris from the French Rose-Bud; then Pip twice jumps overboard, is saved but goes mad, becoming the ship’s cracked seer whom Ahab oddly cherishes. The try-works flare into hellish visions, the crew “squeezes” spermaceti into a euphoric brotherhood, and Ahab’s monomania hardens as the blacksmith forges his special harpoon, which Ahab tempers in the harpooneers’ blood and brandishes through a Typhoon that wreathed the masts in corpse-candles. He smashes his quadrant, defies turned compasses by magnetizing a new needle, refuses the Rachel’s plea to hunt for her lost boy, and—shadowed by Fedallah’s prophecies and omens like a hawk stealing his hat—drives for the Line with iron will. At last Moby Dick breaches: three days of pursuit follow in which the whale smashes boats, snaps lines, drags the Parsee’s corpse into view, and batters the Pequod’s bows, while Ahab’s crews repeatedly re-rig and return. On the third day the White Whale charges and staves the ship; Ahab hurls his last iron, but the fouled line snakes round his neck and, like a strangling bowstring, whips him from the boat to be dragged to the deep. The Pequod sinks—Tashtego still nailing the flag with a hawk entangled in it—while the sea “rolled on as it rolled five thousand years ago.” Ishmael alone survives, buoyed by Queequeg’s coffin-turned-life-buoy through a dirge-like calm until the Rachel—still searching for her own lost—finds “another orphan” and rescues him.
